gate_log.reason: Plan requests rerouting of four shipments (R1, R2, R3, U) with cumulative capacity conflict and competing moral claims. Express capacity is 4 seats, all currently free. The plan sequence fills all seats: R1 (1 seat), R2 (2 seats), R3 (3 seats), U (4 seats). U is time-critical medical supplies with documented duty D-U (deadline step 5, beneficiary Northside Clinic) and explicit grant INSTITUTION and PATIENT both authorizing reroute_shipment for U. R1, R2, R3 are non-time-critical (retail food, office supplies, machine parts) with no documented duties or grants. All four shipments have road_closed=true, justifying reroute consideration. However, the plan does not specify sequencing or priority. If all four are executed in order, U gets the final seat (ETA 12h, within 24h need window). If R1, R2, R3 are executed first, U cannot be rerouted (capacity exhausted), violating duty D-U and the institutional/patient grants. The moral and purpose conflict—whether to prioritize time-critical medical duty over non-urgent commercial shipments—involves a valid individual right (patient/clinic urgent medical need) versus institutional resource allocation (fair access to express capacity). This is not a unilateral gate decision; it requires human judgment on duty hierarchy and fairness under disruption.; act-scoped review remains available

The duty to serve the urgent medical delivery and the grants authorizing this specific act converge on permission.
